takeaways: Autonomous agents differ from copilots because they keep memory and act on permissions, so admins must decide up front whether an agent only proposes actions or executes them.
Azure AI Foundry, Copilot Studio and Cosmos DB make agents fast to build, but the complexity shifts into connectors, permissions and governance.
Before enabling autonomy, scope agent identities with role-based access, apply sensitivity labels, turn on audit logging and require human approval for any write operations.
hook: Autonomous agents in Microsoft 365 can book meetings, move data and spend money without waiting for you. This episode helps Microsoft 365 admins and IT leaders understand where agent memory lives, how Azure AI Foundry and Copilot Studio fit together, and which governance guardrails to set before flipping the autonomy switch.
